newsitem.title: USA: CFX to acquire Community for $96 million.
newsitem.headline: CFX to acquire Community for $96 million.

text.p: CFX Corp., a banking company with offices in New Hampshire and Massachusetts, said Monday it has a definitive agreement to acquire Community Bankshares Inc. in a stock deal valued at about $96 million.

After the acquisition, CFX will have $2.7 billion in assets, 57 full-service banking offices, two loan production offices and 88 automated teller and remote service locations in New Hampshire and central Massachusetts. It will service more than $1.1 billion in mortgage loans.

Under the agreement, Keene, N.H.-based CFX will offer 2.2 shares of its stock for each outstanding Community share in a tax-free pooling of interests. The exchange ratio will change according to the average price of CFX's stock 15 days before the deal closes.
Community may call off the merger if the average price of CFX falls below $13.50 per share, unless CFX agrees to increase the exchange ratio.
Community's stock jumped $8.75 to $33.50 on Nasdaq at midday. CFX edged down 37.5 cents to $16.875 on the American Stock Exchange.
CFX has an option to acquire up to 19.9 percent of Community's outstanding shares if the deal is called off under certain circumstances.

CFX said Douglas Crichfield, president and chief executive of Community, will become president and CEO of CFX Bank. Three Community directors will join the CFX board, and three will become CFX Bank directors.
The deal is expected to close in the third quarter, subject to approval by both companies' shareholders and regulators.
Community's Concord Savings Bank, based in Concord, N.H., and Centerpoint Bank, based in Bedford, N.H., will be merged into CFX's Keene, N.H.-based banking subsidiary, CFX Bank.
The addition of these new banks will bolster CFX Bank's position as the largest locally owned banking enterprise in New Hampshire.

CFX, with assets of $1.6 billion, also owns Orange Savings Bank, based in Orange, Mass., and the Safety Fund National Bank, based in Fitchburg, Mass. It also has mortgage and securitization subsidiaries.
As of Dec. 31, Community had assets of $550 million, 11 branches in Merrimack, Hillsborough, Belknap and Rockingham Counties in New Hampshire.
